continuity_scope: Conan the Barbarian, 1982 theatrical feature-film continuity only. This pass uses the American Film Institute Catalog's original-film record and AFI Movie Club context; it does not merge Robert E. Howard prose, comic, 1984 sequel, 2011 film, game, or any other Conan continuity.
work_or_witnesses: Conan the Barbarian, 1982 theatrical feature film
coverage_rule: Include every individually named dramatic character identified in the AFI original-film cast list: Conan, Thulsa Doom, King Osric, Valeria, Rexor, and Subotai. Cimmerians, cults, magic, roles, artifacts, places, gods, philosophies, unnamed collective categories, and the generically credited witch/princess remain terms or omissions.
omissions: Generically credited roles such as the witch and princess are not treated as personal names; all other cast, groups, named places, spells, objects, and plot events remain omitted unless claim-specific official evidence is available.
Robert E. Howard's stories, comics, Conan the Destroyer (1984), the 2011 reboot, games, and other continuities are separate witnesses.

The selected AFI record supplies R-rated original-film metadata and a vengeance/snake-cult premise, but this research does not add specific enslavement, sexual violence/coercion, nudity/body portrayal, killing, injury, race/ethnicity, or adaptation-difference details without a precise primary scene/screenplay locator.
Cimmerian, barbarian, cult, and evil/sinister labels are source-fiction descriptors and are not mapped to real peoples, religions, ethnicities, or moralized body categories.
uncertainties: AFI gives cast-credit names for all six included individuals, but the accessible official premise gives narrative detail only for Conan and the sinister snake-cult leader played by James Earl Jones. Other records therefore intentionally contain only credit-supported identity.
No complete authorized screenplay or scene/timecode was accessed; no relationship is inferred from cast proximity or later-franchise knowledge.
The film's 1982 R rating signals adult content context but cannot, by itself, substantiate any particular sensitive-content event.
AFI history records the production's rights-development relationship to Robert E. Howard stories. That is production history, not evidence that film characterization equals any prose/comic version.
evidence_basis: American Film Institute authoritative original-film catalog and AFI Movie Club material only; no fan wiki, Wikipedia, unofficial screenplay, uninspected film frame, or franchise recap is used.
